notation.meaning: Vectors (e.g. columns of a data matrix)
Vector in the null space when $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}$
Non-labor income, labor income and total income ($T = NI + S$) in the example

blocks.md: A set of variables is linearly independent if none of them can be built by mixing the others. If one is just a combination of the rest — total income equal to labor plus non-labor income — it adds no new information. Rank counts how many genuinely independent columns a matrix has. When the rank falls short of the number of columns, different coefficient combinations give identical predictions, so a regression cannot tell them apart.

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.md: It is the precise condition behind identification and the dummy variable trap.
— no vector can be written as a combination of the others.
The **rank** of $A$ is the number of linearly independent columns (equivalently rows), which is the dimension of its [Column Space](note:column-space).
The **null space** is $\{\mathbf{x}: A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}\}$; its dimension is the nullity. For $A$ with $k$ columns:
Full column rank ($\mathrm{rank} = k$) means the null space is just $\{\mathbf{0}\}$: different coefficient vectors always produce different $A\mathbf{x}$. That is precisely identification.

| Fact | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| $\mathrm{rank}(A) \leq \min(\text{rows}, \text{cols})$ | Need $N \geq K$ to have full column rank |
| $\mathrm{rank}(\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X}) = \mathrm{rank}(\mathbf{X})$ | $\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X}$ invertible iff $\mathbf{X}$ has full column rank |
| $\mathrm{rank}(AB) \leq \min(\mathrm{rank}A, \mathrm{rank}B)$ | Products can only lose rank |
| Idempotent $A$: $\mathrm{rank}(A) = \mathrm{trace}(A)$ | Degrees of freedom ([Trace of a Matrix](note:trace-of-a-matrix)) |
Columns $[\mathbf{1},\ NI,\ S,\ NI + S]$ with four observations: the fourth column equals the second plus the third, so the rank is **3**, not 4. $\mathbf{x} = (0, 1, 1, -1)'$ is in the null space.

- **Nonlinear** dependence does not reduce rank: $x$ and $x^2$ are fine together.
- High correlation between columns is *near*-dependence (multicollinearity): rank is still full, but estimates become imprecise.

- **Econometrics**: [Full Rank and Identification](note:full-rank-and-identification); the dummy variable trap in [Indicator Variables](note:indicator-variables); $\mathrm{rank}(\mathbf{M}) = n - K$ in [Projection Matrix and Residual Maker](note:projection-matrix-and-residual-maker).
